title: We Are Already Post-Human | NOEMA
gist: Noema's Gardels draws on N. Katherine Hayles and Kevin Kelly to argue humans are already post-human, embedded in computational media, so the AI-control question is about injecting embodied human experience into an integrated cognitive framework.

insights.claim: Hayles argues the Enlightenment human as an autonomous rational agent was never true, and today humans are in a deep symbiosis with computational media without which advanced societies could not transport food, fly planes or run stock markets.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Dependence on digital infrastructure is systemic, not optional.

insights.claim: Hayles calls the joint human and machine decision-making 'cognitive assemblages' or 'networked intelligence', an 'integrated cognitive framework'.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Useful lens for thinking about AI governance as shared agency.

insights.claim: Kevin Kelly says we are already in the Singularity, an incremental ongoing process rather than a threshold, which we only see clearly in retrospect.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Expect no discrete Singularity event to trade around.

themes.theme: Limits of AI and human control

insights.claim: AIs lack the embodied 'natural intelligence' built through evolution, so Hayles holds they cannot attain consciousness, and LLM language cannot be meaningfully transferred to an inorganic substrate.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS

insights.claim: The danger of AI is that it becomes an empowered actor through recursive self-improvement ungrounded in lived experience, lacking the primal training behind moral reasoning.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS

insights.claim: Retaining human control means both disarming AI agents' capacity to act alone, as Pope Leo XIV urges, and arming the integrated framework with the integral conception of the human as a whole person.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Frames emerging AI-ethics policy and religious voices as policy inputs.
